title: Capacity Sprint Ledger — microbudget & HC swapbook (Q3 scenario)
content:
Purpose: quick-reference playbook for capacity-constrained Q3 scenarios where we must pair short-term microbudgets (3–12 weeks) with headcount swaps and price levers to protect margin. Intended consumers: finance leads, ops PMs, SRE on-call, and GTM lead for pricing actions.

High-level objectives:
- Avoid SLA breach while maintaining run-rate margin >= target band.
- Create a repeatable swapbook for shifting labor/contractor spend into burst GPU reserve and vice versa.
- Provide a fast, friction-light sensitivity check for pricing tests that can be executed in <24h to inform sales and CS credit decisions.

Key inputs (single-sheet reference):
- Token demand forecast (3w/12w) by segment (PLG, mid-market, enterprise)
- Active commitments and reserved GPU capacity by region (US, EU, APAC)
- Current token mix by model-class (gpt-like-8k, open-16k, embed-2) and per-token unit costs
- Labor cost ladder (fte vs contractor hourly) and ramp-up windows (2w contractor, 6w hire)
- Existing promo/credit queues and outstanding contractual SLAs

Assumptions (explicit):
- Spot GPU availability can be increased 10–30% on 48–72h notice at premium cost (cost multiplier range: 1.15–1.45).
- Contractor surge can fill 60% of short-term ops work within 2w at blended fully-loaded rate roughly 1.6x hourly of FTE.
- Pricing elasticity: small enterprise tilts (+3–8% price) reduce token volume 0–4% in first 4w; PLG price tilts >5% cause steep adoption drop. (see sensitivity matrix below).

Swapbook rules (operational guardrails):
1) Approval thresholds: any swap that moves >$100k/month of spend requires finance+GTM verbal OK. <$100k authorized by finance lead.
2) Swap priority order: 1) reallocate contractor hours -> burst GPU reserve; 2) reassign non-customer-facing engineering capacity (temp) -> capacity ops; 3) defer noncritical infra spend.
3) Minimum runway requirement: maintain 6w of burst reserve credit when customer SLA risk > medium.
4) Reversal window: all swaps tagged for automated reversal evaluation at 4w and 12w.

Pricing sensitivity quick matrix (how to run):
- Step A: pick candidate customer segment and model-class mix.
- Step B: apply three price scenarios: conservative +2%, tactical +5%, aggressive +10%.
- Step C: run demand delta assumptions (conservative 0–1% drop, tactical 1–3%, aggressive 3–8%).
- Step D: translate to revenue delta and unit-cost delta (account for burst GPU premium and contractor substitution).
- Output: net margin delta and break-even weeks for swap to pay back.

Sample back-of-envelope table (example numbers for a small enterprise cohort):
- Baseline ARR contribution (12w cadence): $420k; unit margin 28%
- Tactical price +5% -> projected volume -2% -> revenue +3% -> margin +1.6 percentage points when not using burst GPUs.
- If we simultaneously fund 20% extra capacity via spot (cost multiplier 1.3) and shift 200 contractor hours into ops (~$32k), margin changes to -3.5 percentage points. Break-even at 7.6 weeks if price hold persists.

Runbook: what to do when capacity hits trigger levels
- Trigger check (SRE): token queue latency > SLO for two consecutive 1h blocks OR utilization >85% sustained for 6h -> notify finance+ops (Slack channel #capacity-emergency).
- Finance: run quick sensitivity (spreadsheet tab: "+5% test") and surface recommended net action (2 options: price tilt +5% or initiate swapbook A).
- GTM: prepare customer comms templates (two versions: opt-in price protection for enterprise; credit offer for PLG heavy users).
- Ops: initiate contractor surge + spot reservation within approval thresholds. Tag all transactions with "capacity-sprint-Q3" for reconciliation.

Spreadsheet tabs to include (sheet naming conventions):
- inputs_forecast_3w (single source of truth demand)
- capacity_inventory_by_region
- labor_heatmap (fte vs contractor availability)
- pricing_sensitivity_runs (scenario table)
- swapbook_actions (approval log + expected payback)
- reconciliations (actual vs plan, weekly)

Approval checklist (pre-swap):
- [ ] Confirm trigger met (SRE)
- [ ] Run sensitivity table (Finance) and capture results in sheet
- [ ] GTM ok for customer-facing price movement? (yes/no)
- [ ] Legal check for contracted accounts impacted (if >$50k ARR exposed)
- [ ] Tagging policy set for billing and accounting

Open questions / debate items (notes to self):
- Should we centralize contractor surge purchasing (finance) or keep it locally owned by ops? Centralization saves margin negotiation but slows deployment.
- How aggressively should we expose price tests publicly vs targeted? Targeted reduces churn risk but increases segmentation complexity.
- Can we pre-negotiate short spot blocks with our cloud partners to reduce premium? (ask infra partnerships).

Next steps (owners and ETA):
- Build template spreadsheet and link to Confluence (Asha, 2026-02-28)
- Mock run of +5% pricing sensitivity on historical May–Aug 2025 token data (Marco, 2026-03-05)
- Draft customer comms templates (Sana, 2026-02-25)
- Ops to surface contractor vendor SLA and 48h provisioning worksheet (Omar, 2026-03-01)

Appendix: quick formulas (for sheet):
- projected_revenue = baseline_revenue * (1 + price_delta) * (1 + demand_delta)
- incremental_capacity_cost = baseline_capacity_cost * capacity_multiplier
- net_margin_after_swap = (projected_revenue - incremental_capacity_cost - additional_labor_costs) / projected_revenue

Tone: working playbook — intentionally concise, action-oriented, includes unresolved questions. Archive as draft after two live episodes and then finalize as a repeatable protocol.
